findings.title: Team permission check uses AND instead of OR, locking out team admins
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Since `isTeamAdmin` already returns true for ADMIN *and* OWNER roles, requiring both predicates means only team OWNERS pass; team ADMINs are rejected with FORBIDDEN even though the variable name and intent say otherwise. It should be `||` (or just `isTeamAdmin`). Consequence: team admins cannot add guests to team bookings they manage.

findings.title: Calendar/video update uses the requester's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` build the EventManager from the *logged-in* user, but `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` must operate on the organizer's calendar/video integration (the references belong to `booking.user`). When an attendee or a team admin/owner adds guests, the requester has no credentials for the organizer's Google/Outlook calendar or video app, so the external calendar invite is never updated (or the wrong account is targeted) while the DB and emails say it succeeded. The handler already fetches `booking.user.credentials` (line 38) but never uses it.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the unfiltered input list, not the actually-added guests
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` is the filtered list (existing attendees and blacklisted addresses removed), but `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw input. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, membership in that array decides whether an attendee gets a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (new-booking confirmation) or the `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` update. So if the caller re-submits an email that is already an attendee, that existing attendee receives a brand-new booking-confirmation email instead of the "guests added" notice. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

findings.title: Server does not de-duplicate emails within the submitted guest list
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` only filters guests against existing `booking.attendees` and the blacklist; duplicates *within* the `guests` array pass through and are inserted via `createMany`. The uniqueness check only exists client-side in `AddGuestsDialog`, so any direct tRPC call (or a race between two calls) creates multiple Attendee rows with the same email for one booking, which then produces duplicate emails and duplicate entries in the attendee list/ICS. De-duplicate (e.g. `new Set`, case-normalized) on the server.

findings.title: No upper bound on the number of guests allows mass-mail abuse
findings.body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` accepts an unbounded array. Any authenticated user is the organizer of their own bookings, so they can call `bookings.addGuests` with thousands of arbitrary addresses; the handler then creates an Attendee row per address and `sendAddGuestsEmails` sends a Cal.com-branded confirmation email with an ICS invite to each one. This turns the endpoint into an email relay/spam vector from Cal.com's sending domain and can also blow up the single DB write and the email queue. Add a `.max(...)` limit (and ideally rate limiting).

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings
findings.body: Every other sender in this file guards with `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)`, but `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no `eventTypeMetadata` and sends unconditionally. Event types that have explicitly disabled standard host/attendee emails (e.g. because the organizer sends their own via workflows) will still blast organizer and attendee emails when guests are added, violating that configuration.

findings.title: Newly added guests receive the full attendee list even when seatsShowAttendees is false
findings.body: `new AttendeeScheduledEmail(calendarEvent, attendee)` is called without the `showAttendees` argument (compare `sendScheduledSeatsEmails`, which passes it). For seated event types with `seatsShowAttendees: false`, the email/ICS sent to a newly added guest will disclose the names and email addresses of all other attendees, leaking personal data that the event type is configured to hide.

findings.title: Guests added to seated bookings get no BookingSeat record and bypass seatsPerTimeSlot
findings.body: Attendees are inserted directly with `attendees.createMany` without creating the corresponding `BookingSeat` row and without checking `eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot`. For seated events the rest of the product (seat-reference based cancel/reschedule links, seat availability counting, success page) keys off `BookingSeat`; attendees created here will have no seat reference, so they cannot cancel/reschedule their seat and the seat capacity can be exceeded. Either reject seated bookings in this handler or create the seat references.

findings.title: CalendarEvent is built without `team`, so team hosts are never notified
findings.body: The `evt` object omits `team`, yet `sendAddGuestsEmails` loops over `calendarEvent.team?.members` to notify co-hosts. Because `team` is always undefined here, that loop is dead code and additional hosts of team/round-robin events never learn that guests were added. Populate `evt.team` (as `editLocation`/booking flows do) or drop the loop.

findings.title: No validation of booking status; guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/past bookings
findings.body: The handler only checks existence and permissions. A cancelled, rejected or already-finished booking will still get new attendees, a calendar-attendee update and "your event" confirmation emails to the new guests. The UI hides the action for cancelled bookings, but the tRPC mutation is reachable directly. Reject bookings whose status is not ACCEPTED/PENDING (and optionally bookings in the past).

findings.title: Email failures are swallowed with console.log and the error is discarded
findings.body: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` drops `err` entirely and uses `console.log` instead of the shared `logger` used elsewhere in the codebase. If guest notification emails fail there is no actionable signal (no stack, no bookingId), making production incidents undebuggable while the mutation still reports success.

findings.title: findFirstOrThrow with `booking.userId || 0` yields an opaque 500 for bookings without a user
findings.body: When `booking.userId` is null (e.g. dynamic group bookings or bookings whose user was deleted), the query looks up user id 0 and `findFirstOrThrow` raises a Prisma error that surfaces as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a meaningful tRPC error. Handle the null-userId case explicitly (or use the already-included `booking.user` relation).

findings.title: New mutation that mutates bookings and sends email has no tests
findings.body: `addGuestsHandler` contains non-trivial authorization logic (organizer / attendee / team admin), filtering/blacklisting, attendee creation and email+calendar side effects, but no unit or integration test is added in this PR. The permission bug on line 46 (AND vs OR) and the unfiltered `guests` passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails` are exactly the kind of regressions a handler test would catch.

findings.title: Stale "emails must be unique and valid" error persists after a successful add
findings.body: `onSuccess` resets `multiEmailValue` and closes the dialog but never clears `isInvalidEmail`. If the user first submits an invalid entry and then a valid one, the error banner stays in state and is displayed again the next time the dialog is opened, even though the input is empty. Reset `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` in `onSuccess` (and on successful validation in `handleAdd`).

findings.title: Error toast shows raw tRPC error codes and the fallback message is unreachable
findings.body: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`` is always a non-empty string, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` can never fall back to the friendly copy, and users are shown technical strings such as "FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission" or "undefined: ..." when `err.data` is missing. Translate known message keys and fall back to `t("unable_to_add_guests")` when the code/message is not user-facing.

findings.title: Component inside packages/ui imports the package's own barrel, creating a circular dependency
findings.body: `import { Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip } from "@calcom/ui";` is a self-import of the package root, which `packages/ui/index.tsx` in turn re-exports (`export { default as MultiEmail } from "./form/MultiEmailLazy"`). Circular barrel imports can resolve to `undefined` component references depending on module evaluation order and bloat the lazy chunk this file is meant to keep small. Import from the relative component paths (`../components/button`, `../components/form`, `../components/icon/Icon`, `../components/tooltip`) as other internal files do.

findings.title: Label `htmlFor="emails"` points at a non-existent input id
findings.body: The `<label htmlFor="emails">` has no matching element with `id="emails"` (the rendered `EmailField`s get generated ids and are passed `label={<></>}`), so clicking the label does nothing and screen readers announce the inputs without a label. Either give the first input that id or associate labels per field.
